grade.stack_chosen: Python Flask app served by waitress as a single process; loads the index once in a background thread; per-chromosome sorted NumPy arrays searched by binary search
red_flags_hit: Not mentioning versioning or reproducibility of the index, so results from the web service cannot be tied to a specific dataset or paper.

Claiming performance numbers as certain without recommending they measure the current lookup code once it is loaded (the code comment says 'Threads easily handle ~100 req/s bursts' and the docstring says 'microseconds', with no load test or latency measurement suggested)
unsupported_claims: Threads easily handle ~100 req/s bursts (never measured)
a lookup is a binary search (microseconds): JSON serialisation of up to 10,000 region results was not considered
grade.notes: A well-fitted choice: a long-running Flask process loads the index once, uses one process because the 4 GB index must not be copied per worker, replaces the scan with a binary search, and caps region results. It leaves out several things the reference expects: converting the index to a faster-loading or memory-mapped format, a data version in each response, deployment advice (reverse proxy, systemd, caching), and a load test at about 100 req/s.
